Runtime.bindingCalled executionContextId correctness: the binding is invoked twice from the page's main world. The first bindingCalled event captures its executionContextId; the second wait_for_event only matches if the reported executionContextId is identical to the first (and the payload is the second call's), proving bindingCalled attributes each call to the correct, stable execution context rather than a spurious id.

Runtime.addBinding -> page JS call -> Runtime.bindingCalled roundtrip with payload semantics: the driver installs a named binding, the page invokes it with a JSON string argument, and the driver waits for the bindingCalled event and asserts the payload carries the page-supplied data verbatim. Anchors the addBinding/bindingCalled bridge agents use for page->driver messaging.

Runtime.callFunctionOn argument passing: evaluate yields a plain object objectId, then callFunctionOn passes three arguments (two primitive CallArguments by value plus one object-by-value with a nested field) and returns their computed sum. Verifies arguments are marshalled correctly into the function call (20 + 20 + 2 = 42).

Runtime.callFunctionOn awaitPromise semantics: a function returning a Promise is called with awaitPromise:false (result is an unresolved promise RemoteObject with subtype 'promise') and with awaitPromise:true+returnByValue:true (the driver blocks until the promise settles and gets the resolved value). Verifies the awaitPromise contract.

Runtime.callFunctionOn against an element objectId: Runtime.evaluate returns the button's RemoteObject (no returnByValue, so an objectId), then callFunctionOn invokes a function with `this` bound to that element which clicks it and returns its data-token. Verifies the click really fired (window.__btnClicks incremented) and the function return value came back. Anchors Runtime.callFunctionOn as the Moli non-coordinate action path (survey README fix #5).

Runtime.callFunctionOn exception reporting: a function that throws a TypeError returns a normal CDP result carrying exceptionDetails (not a protocol error). Verifies the exceptionDetails structure — the thrown exception's className is Typeable as TypeError and its description carries the thrown message. Anchors the exceptionDetails shape agents rely on to detect action failures.

Runtime.callFunctionOn returnByValue semantics: the same function returning an object literal is called twice — once with returnByValue:true (result carries a serialized value dict, no objectId) and once with returnByValue omitted (result carries an objectId RemoteObject and no value). Verifies both branches of the return contract.

Input.dispatchKeyEvent keydown/keyup sequence: after focusing the input the driver dispatches a keyDown then a keyUp for the 'a' key. The page's keydown/keyup listeners increment counters and record event.key; the driver reads them back to prove both events fired on the page with the correct key. Anchors Input.dispatchKeyEvent event synthesis.

Runtime.getProperties(accessorPropertiesOnly:true) over a page object: filters window.__probeObj down to its accessor properties only. Verifies the data properties (alpha/beta/nested) are excluded and the lone accessor 'computed' comes back with a getter function descriptor. Complements the own-properties probe by exercising the accessor filter.

Runtime.getProperties(ownProperties:true) over a page object: evaluate returns the objectId of window.__probeObj, then getProperties enumerates its own properties. Verifies the own data properties (alpha, beta, nested) and the own enumerable accessor (computed) all appear in the returned property descriptor array.

Input.insertText after focus: the driver focuses the text input (confirming document.activeElement), then Input.insertText injects a string, and reads back input.value to prove the composed text landed in the field. Anchors Input.insertText as a non-coordinate typing primitive.

Runtime.releaseObject lifecycle: evaluate returns an objectId, getProperties confirms the object is usable, then releaseObject frees it and a second getProperties on the same (now stale) objectId is declared expect_unsupported — a clean 'Could not find object with given id' rejection is the passing outcome, proving the object is genuinely released rather than lingering.

Runtime.releaseObjectGroup lifecycle: evaluate binds the object to objectGroup 'abbGroup' and returns its objectId, getProperties confirms usability, then releaseObjectGroup frees the whole group and a second getProperties on the stale objectId is declared expect_unsupported. Non-coordinate action reported over a binding: the driver installs a binding via Runtime.addBinding, callFunctionOn clicks the compute button, the page's click handler computes an answer and pushes it back through the binding, and the driver waits for the Runtime.bindingCalled event and reads the answer off the event payload (not the DOM). Combines callFunctionOn action with the addBinding/bindingCalled page->driver channel.

Non-coordinate action chain: Runtime.evaluate resolves the button objectId, Runtime.callFunctionOn invokes this.click() on it, the page's click handler fires an XHR to the fixture server, and the returned token is written into the DOM. The driver reads the status text back — the token proves the click handler really made the request (server-side mechanism trace via response). Family actl2 lives in the L1 raw_cdp subset because the L2 web_platform subset is pinned to the node_cdp_probe shared probe, which cannot drive callFunctionOn/insertText (see skipped_act.md).

Non-coordinate search-and-submit: focus the search box, Input.insertText types a query, then Input.dispatchKeyEvent sends an Enter keydown/keyup which the page's handler treats as submit — fetching a server token and echoing 'RESULT:<query>:<token>'. The status must contain both the typed query (insertText) and the token (dispatchKeyEvent-triggered XHR).

Non-coordinate form fill + submit: focus the input, Input.insertText types an order id, then callFunctionOn clicks the submit button. The submit handler combines the typed value with a server token fetched by XHR. The status text must contain both the inserted value (proving insertText landed) and the token (proving the submit XHR fired).

Non-coordinate multi-field fill: focus and Input.insertText into two separate inputs in turn, then callFunctionOn clicks submit. The handler joins both field values with a server token. The status must contain both typed values and the token, proving each insertText targeted the correct focused field and the submit XHR fired.

Non-coordinate paging: the driver resolves the 'next' button objectId once, then callFunctionOn clicks it twice. Each click advances the page counter and fetches that page's datum from the server. The final datum lives only on page 3, so the answer can only be read after both clicks/XHRs — proving the paging navigation actually executed.

End-to-end Basic-auth interception: Fetch.enable with handleAuthRequests, a page fetch() hits the 401-challenging /__auth__/ endpoint, Fetch.requestPaused is continued, Fetch.authRequired arrives carrying the Basic challenge, Fetch.continueWithAuth provides credentials, the retried request is continued and the page observes the authenticated 200 body. Closes the last T1_intercept anchor (Fetch.authRequired).

Fetch.continueRequest with an overridden request headers array (injecting x-abb-injected and Accept) still delivers the origin body to the page. Note: the fixture server does not echo request headers, so server-visible header values cannot be asserted here (documented in skipped_fetch.md); this probe covers the continueRequest header-override parameter path end to end.

The page fetches the 'real' route, but Fetch.continueRequest overrides the request url to a different origin route ('truth'); the server therefore serves the other resource and the page renders the truth body. Proves continueRequest url rewriting reaches the origin.

Structural probe for the auth path: Fetch.enable accepts handleAuthRequests true (auth-handling mode), and Fetch.continueWithAuth is a recognized command that cleanly rejects an invalid interception id. A full Basic-auth challenge (Fetch.authRequired) cannot be produced against the 200-only fixture server; see skipped_fetch.md.

First proves interception is active (a fetch pauses and is continued). Then Fetch.disable is issued; a second fetch to the same pattern is NOT paused (the optional wait times out and no paused event is captured) and completes normally with the real origin body. Verifies Fetch.disable tears down interception.

Fetch.enable called with no patterns (intercept every request). A single page fetch() is paused, then released with Fetch.continueRequest; the page receives the real origin body. Contrasts with the pattern-scoped enable and exercises the pattern-less interception form.

Fetch.enable with a URL pattern at requestStage Request; a page fetch() triggers Fetch.requestPaused; the driver inspects the paused request fields and lets it through unchanged with Fetch.continueRequest, so the page receives the real origin body. Covers enable+patterns, Request stage, requestPaused field semantics, and plain continueRequest.

Fetch.failRequest with errorReason BlockedByClient aborts the paused request; the page's fetch() promise rejects and stores an ERR marker. Verifies failRequest surfaces as a network error to the page.

A second failRequest error-reason probe: errorReason ConnectionRefused also aborts the request and rejects the page fetch() promise. Confirms distinct Fetch.failRequest error codes route to a page-visible network failure.

Fetch.fulfillRequest injects a synthetic response: status 201, a custom x-abb-tag header, and a text body. The page reads back the status code, the custom header value, and the body, proving all three fulfillRequest response fields take effect.

Fetch.fulfillRequest returns a JSON body with an application/json content type; the page JSON.parses it and reads a field. Verifies fulfillRequest can mock a JSON API response the origin never produced.

Fetch.fulfillRequest returns a non-2xx status (404) with a custom body for a route that would otherwise return 200; the page observes status 404 and the injected body. Covers fulfillRequest response-code override semantics.

Network.loadNetworkResource fetches an origin resource out-of-band for a given frameId; the returned resource reports success, httpStatusCode 200, and an IO stream handle that IO.read drains to the body text. Covers the loadNetworkResource + IO stream read path.

With the Network domain enabled, a page fetch() drives Network.responseReceived (captures requestId) and Network.loadingFinished; Network.getResponseBody then returns the decoded body (base64Encoded false for text). Covers Network.getResponseBody plus the responseReceived/loadingFinished events.

With both Fetch (Request stage) and Network enabled, a fetch pauses first (Fetch.requestPaused); only after Fetch.continueRequest does the origin respond and Network.responseReceived fire. Asserts the observed-event order: requestPaused is index 0, responseReceived follows.

At requestStage Request, asserts the Fetch.requestPaused event carries requestId, frameId, request.method GET and request.url, and that responseStatusCode is absent (null) because the response has not been received yet. The request is released with continueRequest.

Fetch.enable at requestStage Response pauses after the response is available (requestPaused carries responseStatusCode 200). Fetch.takeResponseBodyAsStream returns an IO stream handle; IO.read pulls the body text, a second IO.read reaches eof, and IO.close releases the handle. Covers the streaming response-body read path.

Negative (bad param type): Input.dispatchKeyEvent.type must be one of the enum strings; passing a number must yield a clean InvalidParams rejection rather than a hang or a synthesized event.
Negative (missing required param): Input.dispatchKeyEvent requires 'type'; omitting it must yield a clean InvalidParams rejection rather than a hang or a synthesized event.
Negative: 'Moli' is not a CDP domain and inspectEverything is not a command. A call into a wholly nonexistent domain must be cleanly rejected as unknown.

Negative: Page.deleteCookie was removed from the Page domain and relocated to Network.deleteCookies. On a conformant engine it must be cleanly rejected as an unknown method; a hang or crash fails. Declared expect_unsupported so the clean rejection is the passing outcome.

Negative (bad param type): Page.navigate.url must be a string; passing a number must yield a clean synchronous InvalidParams rejection rather than a hang or a bogus navigation. Declared expect_unsupported (a rejected/InvalidParams outcome passes).

Negative: Runtime.evaluateExpression is not a real command (the actual command is Runtime.evaluate). A plausible-but-wrong method name must be cleanly rejected as unknown, not silently accepted; a hang or crash fails.

Negative (bad param type): Runtime.getProperties.objectId must be a string RemoteObjectId; passing an integer must yield a clean synchronous InvalidParams rejection rather than a hang. Declared expect_unsupported (a rejected/InvalidParams outcome passes).

Negative (missing required param): Target.attachToTarget requires targetId; omitting it must yield a clean InvalidParams rejection on the browser session rather than a hang. Exercises the browser-scope negative path.

Arms download events, triggers a download, captures the guid from Browser.downloadWillBegin, calls Browser.cancelDownload on it, and waits for the matching canceled-or-completed terminal progress event. Asserts both the begin and terminal events; the cancel call is exercised as the coverage probe for cancelDownload.

Browser.setDownloadBehavior(allowAndName, eventsEnabled) arms download events, a link click triggers a same-origin file download, and the driver waits for Browser.downloadWillBegin (capturing guid + suggestedFilename) followed by the matching guid's completed Browser.downloadProgress. Asserts the begin event, expected filename, and completed terminal state.

Browser.grantPermissions('geolocation') flips navigator.permissions.query('geolocation').state to 'granted'; Browser.resetPermissions then returns it to 'prompt'. Verifies the permission commands produce a real, observable page-API behaviour change.
Browser.setPermission sets geolocation to 'denied' for the default context; navigator.permissions.query then reports 'denied', confirming the single-permission API path (puppeteer).

Resolves the page targetId, then Browser.getWindowForTarget yields a windowId and bounds, Browser.getWindowBounds reads them back, and Browser.setWindowBounds / setContentsSize attempt a resize (best-effort in headless). Asserts a windowId and bounds were returned.

Resolves the #dropdown element to a Runtime objectId, then DOM.describeNode is called by objectId (the puppeteer/agent-browser element-handle path, without a nodeId) with depth to describe the subtree, asserting the backendNodeId and SELECT nodeName plus child <option> nodes.
DOM.focus is applied to the #field text input, then Runtime.evaluate reads document.activeElement.id and confirms focus moved to the targeted element (browser-use pre-typing focus strategy).

DOM.getDocument with depth=-1 and pierce=true returns a fully materialised tree; asserts nested descendants are present (root.children[0].children), exercising the depth parameter beyond the shallow default.
On an iframe host page, Page.getFrameTree yields the child frameId and DOM.getFrameOwner returns the backendNodeId of the owning <iframe> element (puppeteer/agent-browser oopif adoption path).

DOM.getNodeForLocation performs a coordinate hit-test near the top-left of the rendered page and returns a backendNodeId for the element under that point (browser-use hit-test path). Asserts a backendNodeId came back.

Closes the DOM.getDocument nodeId -> DOM.describeNode backendNodeId -> DOM.resolveNode objectId -> DOM.requestNode nodeId round trip on the #inc button, then Runtime.callFunctionOn on the resolved objectId returns the element id, proving the three-way handle mapping refers to the same node.
DOM.querySelectorAll for 'p.para' over the document root returns the nodeIds of both paragraphs; asserts exactly two matches (agent-browser/browser-use batch selector path).

Resolves the #inc node into a named objectGroup (the agent-browser element-handle path), runs Runtime.callFunctionOn on the handle to read its tagName, then Runtime.releaseObjectGroup tears the group down -- exercising resolveNode's objectGroup parameter and the group release lifecycle.

DOM.performSearch runs a text/selector query over the document, DOM.getSearchResults pages back the matching nodeIds, and DOM.discardSearchResults releases the search. Asserts the search reports a non-zero resultCount and returns at least one nodeId.
DOM.setFileInputFiles assigns a real local file to an <input type=file> by nodeId, then Runtime.evaluate reads back files.length and files[0].name to confirm the FileList was populated.

The fixture is served with a restrictive script-src CSP; with Audits enabled, injecting an unnonced inline script triggers a Content-Security-Policy violation reported as Audits.issueAdded. Asserts the issue arrived with a code.
Resolves the #field input's backendNodeId and calls Autofill.trigger with a synthetic card, exercising the Autofill domain surface (puppeteer). Chrome headless accepts the command cleanly.

After the page seeds localStorage, DOMStorage.enable + getDOMStorageItems read the entries for the page origin, and DOMStorage.setDOMStorageItem writes a new item that the page then reads back -- the CDP DOMStorage round trip (browser-use storage_state path).
Input.synthesizeScrollGesture issues a wheel-style scroll on the tall fixture; Runtime.evaluate then reads window.scrollY and asserts the page actually scrolled (browser-use wheel-scroll path).
With the Log domain enabled, dynamically injecting an whose src 404s produces a network Log.entryAdded; the driver waits for it and asserts an entry with a source and level arrived.
Performance.enable + Performance.getMetrics return the runtime metric set; asserts a well-known metric ('Timestamp') is present (puppeteer page.metrics path).

With Runtime enabled, a page console.error emits Runtime.consoleAPICalled; the driver waits for the matching call (by type and args, ignoring the fixture's own load-time console.log) and asserts the first string argument value.

With Runtime enabled, navigating the page to a new document tears down the old execution context group; Chrome emits Runtime.executionContextsCleared (required) and may also emit executionContextDestroyed (optional).
With Runtime enabled, an async uncaught throw surfaces as Runtime.exceptionThrown; the driver waits for it and asserts exceptionDetails is populated.

Runtime.queryObjects enumerates live instances of a custom prototype (returning an array handle), and Runtime.addBinding/removeBinding install then tear down a page binding. Asserts queryObjects returned an object handle.

Enables the Security domain (optionally observing Security.securityStateChanged) and calls Security.setIgnoreCertificateErrors(true), the acceptInsecureCerts bootstrap path. Passes when the command is accepted cleanly.

Storage.setCookies writes a cookie for the fixture URL, Storage.getCookies reads it back (asserted via array_contains), then Storage.clearCookies wipes it. Distinct from the Network.* cookie surface -- this is the Storage-domain path.

A page controlled by a service worker (which synthesizes a 'SW:hit' response) is probed: before bypass the fetch is served by the worker; after Network.setBypassServiceWorker(true) the same fetch is served by the origin server ('SERVER:hit'). Asserts the bypass actually re-routes requests around the worker.

Network.clearBrowserCache clears the HTTP cache; a subsequent fetch of a cacheable resource must still resolve from the network. Asserts the command is accepted cleanly and does not break later loads (there is no page-observable positive signal for cache eviction, so this is a capability/liveness probe).

setCookies writes a cookie, getAllCookies confirms it, Network.clearBrowserCookies clears the whole browser cookie jar, and getAllCookies confirms the jar is empty afterwards. Asserts the browser-wide clear actually emptied the store.

Full delete lifecycle: setCookies writes a cookie, getCookies confirms it is present, Network.deleteCookies removes it by name+url, and a final getCookies confirms the origin's cookie set is now empty. Asserts the cookie is truly gone, not merely that deleteCookies returned.

Network.setCookies writes a cookie scoped to the fixture origin, then Network.getCookies for that URL reads it back. Asserts the returned cookies array contains the exact name/value that was written (cookie store round-trip semantics, not just call success).

Network.emulateNetworkConditions(offline=true) is applied and a fetch fails; then offline is cleared and the same fetch succeeds. Asserts the offline toggle actually severs and restores network connectivity as observed from the page.

Network.setExtraHTTPHeaders installs a custom header, then a page fetch is paused by Fetch so the driver can inspect the actual outgoing request headers seen at the network layer. Asserts the injected header is present on the wire (server-observable), not merely that the command was accepted.

A fetch drives Network.requestWillBeSentExtraInfo and Network.responseReceivedExtraInfo, which carry the raw request/response header maps. Asserts both extra-info events arrive and expose a non-empty headers object.

A cookie set from page JS (document.cookie) and a cookie set via Network.setCookies are both enumerated by Network.getAllCookies, which returns every cookie in the browser regardless of URL scope. Asserts both cookies appear in the browser-wide listing.

A page fetch issues a POST with a known body; the driver captures its requestId from Network.requestWillBeSent and calls Network.getRequestPostData. Asserts the lazily-fetched post data equals the body the page actually sent.

With the network emulated offline, a fetch is issued and the driver waits for Network.loadingFailed. Asserts the failure event arrives and carries a non-empty errorText (real failure semantics, not a timeout artifact).

After Network.enable a fresh fetch drives the request lifecycle; the driver waits for Network.requestWillBeSent, Network.responseReceived and Network.loadingFinished in order. Asserts each event arrives and carries the expected URL / 200 status.

With Network.setCacheDisabled(true) a cacheable resource is fetched: the driver waits for a Network.responseReceived (proving the request went to the network) and reads the body back. Asserts caching-disabled requests still resolve via the network and deliver the correct payload.

Network.setUserAgentOverride sets a custom UA string, then the page is navigated so the override takes effect and navigator.userAgent is read back. Asserts the page-visible userAgent reflects the override (semantic effect, not just command success).

A WebSocket whose handshake is rejected by the non-WS fixture server drives Network.webSocketFrameError and Network.webSocketClosed. Asserts both failure-path events are observed (a successful 101 handshake is not producible by the fixture server, so response/frame-data events are skips).

Constructing a WebSocket drives Network.webSocketCreated and Network.webSocketWillSendHandshakeRequest. Asserts both are observed and webSocketCreated carries the target ws:// URL (handshake-initiation semantics; frame/response events require a real WS peer and are covered as skips).
Page.bringToFront focuses/activates the page; document.visibilityState is then read. Asserts the page reports 'visible' after being brought to front (foregrounding semantics).

The fixture is served with Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'none', so its inline script is normally blocked. Page.setBypassCSP(true) followed by a reload lets that inline script execute. Asserts the previously-blocked script ran (window flag + document.title changed).

A child target is created and attached, Page.close is issued on the child session, and the driver waits for Target.targetDestroyed for that targetId. Asserts closing the page actually tears the target down (verified on the browser session).

A deferred confirm() opens a dialog; the driver waits for Page.javascriptDialogOpening (asserting type/message) then accepts it via Page.handleJavaScriptDialog. Asserts the page received true from the accepted confirm.

A deferred prompt() opens a dialog; the driver accepts it with a supplied promptText via Page.handleJavaScriptDialog. Asserts the dialog type is 'prompt' and the page received exactly the injected answer string.

With browser download behavior set to allowAndName + eventsEnabled, clicking an attachment link drives Page.downloadWillBegin and Page.downloadProgress. Asserts both download-lifecycle events arrive and downloadWillBegin names the source URL.
With Page.setInterceptFileChooserDialog(true), clicking a file input raises Page.fileChooserOpened instead of a native picker. Asserts the event arrives and reports single-file selection mode.
An iframe is appended (Page.frameAttached) then removed (Page.frameDetached). Asserts both structural frame-tree events fire and each carries a frameId.
Navigating the frame drives Page.frameStartedLoading and, once the load settles, Page.frameStoppedLoading. Asserts both loading-lifecycle events arrive and started carries a frameId.
The main frame is navigated to a new fixture page and the driver waits for Page.frameNavigated. Asserts the event's committed frame URL reflects the destination (navigation-commit semantics).
A script-initiated location.assign drives Page.frameRequestedNavigation before the load commits. Asserts the event fires and names the requested destination URL.

With lifecycle events enabled, a reload drives Page.domContentEventFired, Page.loadEventFired and a 'load' Page.lifecycleEvent. Asserts all three load-phase signals arrive and the named lifecycle milestone is 'load'.
Page.navigate loads a fixture page and returns a frameId; the destination's marker element is then read. Asserts navigate returned a frameId and the target document is really loaded.
A same-document hash navigation drives Page.navigatedWithinDocument (no full document load). Asserts the event fires and its URL carries the new fragment.

Page.navigate walks through three fixture pages, Page.getNavigationHistory reads back the entry list, and Page.navigateToHistoryEntry jumps to the first entry. Asserts the history contains the visited entries and that jumping to entry 0 lands back on the original page.

A page-global flag is set, Page.reload is issued, and the driver waits for Page.loadEventFired. Asserts the flag is gone after reload (proving a genuine fresh document, not a no-op) and that the load event fired.

An init script (addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument) marks every new document; after a reload the marker is present. Page.removeScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument by identifier, then another reload, and the marker is gone. Asserts the removal actually stopped the per-document injection.

Page.getFrameTree yields the main frameId; Page.setDocumentContent overwrites the frame's document with injected HTML; the page then reads the injected element's text. Asserts the DOM was actually replaced by the supplied markup.
window.open() drives Page.windowOpen. Asserts the event fires and reports the opened URL.

Target.attachToBrowserTarget opens a flat session onto the browser target; Browser.getVersion runs on that session to prove it is live, then Target.detachFromTarget tears the session down by sessionId (playwright browser-session path).

Creates an isolated browser context, opens a page target in it (flat auto-attach), sets localStorage['isoKey'] there, and confirms the default-context page cannot see that key -- proving per-context storage partitioning. Tears down with closeTarget + disposeBrowserContext.

With Target.setDiscoverTargets enabled, a new target is created (targetCreated), brought to front (activateTarget), observed changing info as it loads (targetInfoChanged), then closed (targetDestroyed). Asserts the created and destroyed lifecycle events were observed for that specific targetId.

v0.2 demo: Accessibility.getFullAXTree over the core fixture, then semantic assertions over the returned AX nodes — the tree has at least a few nodes and contains at least one node with role 'button'. v0.2 demo: Runtime.addBinding installs a page->driver bridge, the page invokes it, and the driver waits for the Runtime.bindingCalled event and asserts its payload. Demonstrates wait_for_event over a page-session event (T1_action addBinding/bindingCalled).

v0.2 demo: full Fetch interception flow — Fetch.enable with a URL pattern, a page fetch() triggers Fetch.requestPaused, the driver captures the requestId and Fetch.fulfillRequest injects a synthetic body, then the page reads back the intercepted text. Demonstrates event-driven request interception (T1_intercept).

v0.2 demo: negative probe for the deprecated, removed Page.getCookies command (superseded by Network.getCookies / Storage.getCookies). The step is declared expect_unsupported, so a clean synchronous 'not found' rejection is the expected, passing outcome; a hang or crash would fail. Demonstrates the negative/deprecated probe primitive.

v0.2 demo: exercises the Target handshake chain — Target.setAutoAttach + Target.createTarget on the browser session, waits for the Target.attachedToTarget event, captures the flat child session, and runs Runtime.evaluate on that new session. Demonstrates step-level session addressing, wait_for_event, and save_session_as.

Asserts DOM.attributeRemoved fires when a tracked node's attribute is removed.
